text:
Aisha: hi everyone — first day here! using a corporate Ubuntu 22.04 laptop. trying to run the onboarding devcontainer but hitting a few things: corp proxy blocks direct downloads, asdf install of python 3.11 times out, and ssh-agent isn't picking up my key for git pushes. any pointers?
Marco: welcome Aisha! for proxy you'll want to set http(s)_proxy in your shell and docker config. did you get the company certificate installed?
Aisha: I installed the root cert per the IT doc but apt still fails on some https endpoints. here's the error when running `asdf install python 3.11.4`:
```
Downloading python-3.11.4.tar.xz... failed (timeout)
Error: could not download from mirror
```
Sam (it-ops): if you're behind an explicit corporate proxy you need to export these env vars for both shell and systemd (for the docker build):
```bash
# ~/.profile or /etc/environment for system-wide
export HTTP_PROXY="http://proxy.corp:8080"
export HTTPS_PROXY="http://proxy.corp:8080"
export NO_PROXY="localhost,127.0.0.1,*.redwood.dev"
```
Also add proxy to Docker Desktop or /etc/systemd/system/docker.service.d/http-proxy.conf for the daemon.
Aisha: ok added those, asdf download progressed further but now fails on building bzip2 dependency. The devcontainer's Dockerfile shows `apt-get install -y libbz2-dev libssl-dev` but apt errors earlier.
Riley (devex): two quick notes: 1) we ship a prebuilt base image on our internal registry for corp networks (registry.redwood.internal/onboarding:latest) — you can point the devcontainer to that to avoid building from scratch. 2) for SSH keys, make sure gnome-keyring or ssh-agent is running and that your key is added: `eval "$(ssh-agent -s)" && ssh-add ~/.ssh/id_ed25519`
Aisha: ssh-add errors: "Could not open a connection to your authentication agent"
Marco: that usually means the agent isn't running in the current shell session. If you're using GNOME on Ubuntu, ensure the keyring is unlocked at login, or start agent manually in your shell rc:
```bash
# add to ~/.bash_profile or ~/.profile
if [ -z "$SSH_AGENT_PID" ]; then
  eval "$(ssh-agent -s)"
  ssh-add ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 || true
fi
```
Also verify `ssh -T git@github.com` after adding the key.
Aisha: thanks — added the snippet and it persisted across restarts. still worried about secrets: where do I store REDWOOD_API_KEY for local dev so it's not checked in?
Riley (devex): we recommend one of these for local dev (ordered by security):
- 1Password CLI (op) and the repo's dev-setup script fetches a short-lived token
- direnv with .envrc sourcing secrets from `~/.secrets` (ensure ~/.secrets is in your dotfiles gitignore)
- store in GNOME keyring / secret-service and use a small wrapper that exports at session start
We don't store tokens in repo files. For CI, we use Vault and inject at runtime.
Aisha: can you show an example direnv .envrc?
Riley (devex): sure — create `~/.secrets/redwood.env` and then in the project `.envrc`:
```bash
# .envrc (project root)
source_env ~/.secrets/redwood.env
export REDWOOD_API_KEY
```
Make sure `~/.secrets/redwood.env` contains `REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_live_...` and is `chmod 600` and added to ~/.gitignore. Then `direnv allow` will load it automatically.
Aisha: that worked. one more oddity: the onboarding README mentions Nix for some devs. do we need to install Nix?
Riley (devex): Nix is optional; some teams use it for reproducible shells. If you prefer Nix, use the multi-user installer and then enable experimental features in flake-enabled projects. But for day-1 it's fine to stick with asdf + apt or the prebuilt image I mentioned.
Sam (it-ops): if you still hit blocked apt endpoints, DM me and I can add exceptions for the onboarding mirrors for your machine ID. Also make sure FIPS/proxy inspection rules aren't breaking TLS — we had one case where the proxy replaced certs and broke gpg key imports.
onboarding-bot: Welcome Aisha! You were added to #new-hires and granted access to the internal onboarding registry and docs: https://redwood.internal/onboarding. Complete the checklist to get your machine exemptions.
Aisha: amazing, everything's green now — devcontainer builds, ssh pushes work, and REDWOOD_API_KEY loads via direnv. I'll open a small docs PR to add the registry fallback and the SSH-agent snippet. :shipit:
